rows: Woman in Profile

Albert Southworth and Josiah Hawes ran the most famous daguerreotype studio in Boston. Their sitters look natural instead of stiff, and this woman in profile, with her hair swept neatly back, shows their quiet style.
What can you tell about her from the way she holds her head?
Study of Clouds

Early film saw blue sky as white, so clouds almost disappeared. Gustave Le Gray found ways to print a dramatic cloudy sky, sometimes using a separate negative, and made some of the first great sky pictures.
What shapes can you see in the clouds?
Saint-Sernin, Toulouse

In 1851 the French government sent five photographers on the Mission Héliographique to photograph historic buildings that needed protecting. Le Gray photographed the great church of Saint-Sernin and its tall octagonal tower.
How many levels can you count in the tower?
The Electric Face

A French doctor named Duchenne used gentle electric currents to make a man's face muscles move so he could study expressions. He found that a real smile uses the muscles around the eyes, which is now called a Duchenne smile. Charles Darwin used his photographs in a book about emotions.
Try a fake smile and then a real one. Can you feel your eyes squeeze in the real one?
The Ramparts of Carcassonne

Le Gray photographed the old walls and towers of the medieval city of Carcassonne in France when they were crumbling. They were restored soon afterward, so pictures like this show the town before repairs.
Count the round towers you can see.
Chouteau's Pond, St. Louis
Thomas Easterly's daguerreotype shows a pond on the edge of St. Louis, Missouri, with horse-drawn wagons along the shore. The pond was drained and built over not long afterward.
What would you see here today if you stood in the same place?
Fourth and Olive Streets, St. Louis
On a corner in St. Louis in 1851, awnings shade the shop windows and a horse-drawn wagon waits in the street. It is one of the earliest photographs of an American city street.
What are the people and horses doing?
Théophile Gautier
Théophile Gautier was a French poet and novelist who believed that beauty was reason enough for art. Charles Nègre photographed him as a thoughtful man with a beard.
What do you think he is looking at?
The Grotto of Egeria, Rome

According to legend, a nymph named Egeria met an ancient Roman king in this shady grotto and gave him advice. Robert MacPherson, a Scottish doctor living in Rome, photographed its mossy stones and trees.
Why do you think people made up a story about a magical cave?
The Roman Arch at Orange
This triumphal arch in the south of France was built about two thousand years ago. Édouard Baldus photographed it with huge paper negatives, so every carved detail shows.
How many archways does it have?
Boulevard Haussmann

In the 1850s and 60s, Paris was torn apart and rebuilt with wide boulevards and tall stone buildings. Charles Marville photographed the new streets in the early morning, with long exposures that left them empty.
Why do you think there are no people in the picture?
Chartres Cathedral, West Front

The Bisson brothers photographed the carvings over the doors of Chartres Cathedral, with Jesus seated in the middle and rows of small figures below. Their sharp pictures let people study the carvings without climbing up.
How many figures can you find carved above the door?
Medinet Habu

Huge carved columns rise at Medinet Habu in Egypt, a temple built for Pharaoh Ramses III more than three thousand years ago. John Beasley Greene was one of the first photographers to carry cameras up the Nile.
How many people holding hands would it take to go around one column?
The Valley of Jehoshaphat, Jerusalem

Auguste Salzmann photographed tombs carved in rock near Jerusalem to prove they were very old. His careful pictures were published in a large book and helped start the study of the city's ancient past.
Find the doorways carved in the cliff.
Mrs. James
A smiling woman in a dark dress stands in a Boston studio. Southworth and Hawes asked their sitters to relax, and it shows.
What do you think made her smile?
